item.title: Millennial Samsung Union Leader’s $26 Billion Bonus Victory Turns to Bitterness
item.description: Avoiding old-school labor ideology, a new generation of tech workers finds itself divided by the AI boom.

item.title: Netflix Viewers Are Abandoning Shows After One Season
item.description: Netflix’s biggest hits are losing more than half of their audience after one season

item.title: 【今朝の5本】仕事を始める前に読んでおきたい厳選ニュース
item.description: ホルムズ海峡、鴻海精密工業、4.7兆円の大型上場、消費税引き下げ、原油相場一変

item.title: Korean Won Edges Higher on First Day of 24-Hour Trading
item.description: The South Korean won inched higher against the dollar as the currency began its first day of 24-hour trading.

item.title: Australia Built a Gas Export Empire. Now the Backlash Is Here
item.description: Australia’s liquefied natural gas exporters should be riding high on a A$20 billion ($14 billion) sales windfall from the conflict in the Middle East. Instead, their good fortune has triggered a wave of public backlash.

item.title: The Supertanker Tycoon Making Millions on Hormuz Shuttle Runs
item.description: Just a few weeks into the war, one of the Persian Gulf’s top oil producers quietly began sneaking its crude out of the Strait of Hormuz. Before long, the covert project became so successful that the United Arab Emirates was already approaching its pre-war rate of flows through the waterway by the time the US and Iran signed their interim peace deal.

item.title: Alibaba Gets Reprieve on Lobbying Ban Tied to DoD Blacklist
item.description: A federal judge ordered the Pentagon to give Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. a reprieve from a law that caused all of its lobbyists to drop it as a client while she considers the constitutionality of the measure, in a case set to test the US’s ability to curtail Chinese companies’ activities.

item.title: EasyJet Agrees to Castlelake’s Latest Bid Topping £5 Billion
item.description: EasyJet Plc agreed in principle to a takeover offer of more than £5 billion from Castlelake LP, which swooped in as the UK budget carrier was reeling from soaring jet fuel prices and suppressed demand after the Iran war.

item.title: Chile’s Economy Rebounding in June, Quiroz Tells La Tercera
item.description: Chile’s economy reached a turning point in June and will mount a recovery in the second half of the year, Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz said in an interview published on Sunday.

item.title: Universal’s Latest ‘Minions’ Delivers $64 Million in Film Debut
item.description: Minions & Monsters, the seventh film in the animated franchise depicting the yellow, mischievous creatures who speak in expressive gibberish, was the highest-grossing movie over the July 4 holiday weekend, with $61.4 million in US and Canadian box office sales.

item.title: Drivers Shun Premium Gas in Favor of Regular as Prices Bite
item.description: Drivers across the US, including some behind the wheel of performance vehicles, are switching from premium gasoline to regular in a search for savings as fuel prices remain elevated.

item.title: New York Thunderstorms Raise Flood Risk as Heat Dissipates in US
item.description: New York City will have a cooler, soggier Sunday now that the massive heat dome across the US East that taxed power grids and snarled transit has started to crack, but temperatures in Washington and points south will still remain sultry through Sunday.

item.title: SK Hynix Seeks Access to AI Investors in $29 Billion US Listing
item.description: This week’s $29 billion US stock-market listing for SK Hynix Inc. may be the biggest-ever first-time share sale by a foreign company, but it isn’t just about raising cash. It’s also about competing in the hottest corner of the global stock market — memory chips used in AI computing.

item.title: What’s Happening in EM: Carry Traders Shift Away From Dollar
item.description: This week, Vinicius Andrade joins Kelsey Butler to discuss how emerging-market traders are increasingly turning to currencies from the euro to the Australian dollar to fund bets in the developing world as the US dollar roars back.

item.title: Carry Traders Shift Away From Dollar for Emerging-Market Bets
item.description: Emerging-market traders are increasingly turning to currencies from the euro to the Australian dollar to fund bets in the developing world as the US dollar roars back.

item.title: South Korea Eyes Growth Fund From Chip Tax Windfall, Yonhap Says
item.description: South Korea plans to create an investment fund using tax revenue from its burgeoning semiconductor industry to finance long-term economic growth, Yonhap News reported Sunday citing the presidential chief of staff.

item.title: Germany Plans to Boost 2027 Borrowing as Tax Revenue Falls Short
item.description: Germany plans to increase net new borrowing for 2027 to €118 billion ($135 billion), about 7% more than projected in April.

item.title: OPEC+ Ratifies Planned Oil Quota Hike as Gulf Flows Rebound
item.description: Major OPEC+ members agreed another modest increase to their collective oil-production quotas for next month, adding to the prospect of more supply eventually hitting the market if a US-Iran peace pact can stick.

item.title: India Tells Meta to Remove Child Abuse Content from Instagram
item.description: India notified Meta Platforms Inc. that it needs to remove sexual content involving children from its platforms including Instagram, marking the latest regulatory headache for the US tech giant.

item.title: OPEC+ to Ratify Planned Oil Quota Hike as Gulf Flows Resume
item.description: OPEC+ has a preliminary agreement for another modest oil quota increase in August, delegates said, raising the prospect of more supply eventually hitting the market again if a US-Iran peace pact can stick.

item.title: Nvidia Supplier Hon Hai’s Sales Beat on Continued AI Demand
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s server assembly partner Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. reported a bigger-than-expected 40% jump in quarterly sales and said AI demand is growing further.

item.title: BOK Warns of Risks From Single-Stock Leveraged ETFs: Yonhap
item.description: The Bank of Korea warned that single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. could deepen market concentration, amplify volatility and intensify one-way trading flows, according to a local report.

item.title: Fewer Ships Transiting Hormuz Along Oman Coast After U-Turns
item.description: The number of vessels sailing through the Strait of Hormuz along the Omani coast fell to a trickle on Sunday, a day after several exiting along that route made sharp reversals, underscoring Iran’s continued efforts to maintain its grip on the waterway.

item.title: Modi’s Biofuel Push Comes Under Pressure as Motorists Protest
item.description: Indian motorists will gather in New Delhi on Sunday, in the first major protest against a flagship biofuel program intended to reduce crude imports and support farm incomes.

item.title: Wang Yi Says China Welcomes Stronger European Business Relations
item.description: China welcomes deeper cooperation with Swedish and European businesses, which will benefit all parties involved, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said in a meeting with Investor AB Chairman Jacob Wallenberg in Stockholm on July 4, according to a statement from the ministry on Sunday.

item.title: NZ Pledges Trade Talks With Brazil, Europe Within Five Years
item.description: New Zealand’s governing National Party will begin negotiations for seven new trade deals within five years should it win the November election, Trade Minister Todd McClay said.

item.title: Investors Looking for Shelter From AI Storm Are Turning to India
item.description: After losing out big on the global AI rally, Indian equities are regaining the attention of investors seeking to weather the latest market turbulence.

item.title: Trump Ramps Up War on Regulations With 702 Cuts in Pipeline
item.description: The Trump administration is stepping up its efforts to cut red tape across the federal government, releasing a regulatory plan that would eliminate 702 existing administrative rules.

item.title: Germany’s Second Chance for Growth Rebound Starts Now
item.description: German data in the coming week showing the cumulative impact of the Iran war will set the stage for the government’s latest bid to awaken animal spirits in Europe’s biggest economy.

item.title: Venezuela’s Official Death Toll From Quake Rises to Almost 3,000
item.description: Venezuela‘s official death toll from last week’s twin earthquakes rose to almost 3,000 on Saturday.
